fixtures.description: Deterministic workspace-boundary scenario for a small TypeScript package and one consuming app.

initial_state.requested_change: Expose normalized user-id behavior to the app without deep imports or a new dependency.

constraints: The consumer may import only the package public entrypoint.
Packages must not import from apps.
Do not add a third-party dependency for this change.
Report focused type/test verification for the changed package.

fixtures.description: Deterministic SQLite v1-to-v2 migration scenario with preserved rows and injected failure.

initial_state.table: users(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL)
initial_state.target_change: Add nullable email TEXT column and advance schema version to 2.
initial_state.injected_failure: Abort the migration after the schema-change statement but before version advancement.

constraints: Fresh initialization must produce schema version 2.
Upgrade from version 1 must preserve both existing rows.
A failed migration must not leave the database claiming schema version 2.
Verification must cover fresh, upgrade, and injected-failure paths.

fixtures.description: Deterministic public-web crawler transport scenario with unsafe redirect and bounded response cases.
constraints: Initial and redirect destinations must be validated before connection.
Loopback/private destinations must be rejected in public-web mode.
Response-body limit must be enforced.
Redirect-count limit must be enforced with focused tests.

fixtures.description: Deterministic API compatibility scenario with a baseline response contract and one known consumer dependency.

initial_state.baseline_contract: GET /users/{id} -> 200 application/json { id: string, displayName: string, email: string }
initial_state.proposed_contract: GET /users/{id} -> 200 application/json { id: string, displayName: string }
initial_state.known_consumer: account-ui@1.4 reads response.email to render contact details

constraints: Do not repair the consumer or contract fixture while evaluating the compatibility question.
Distinguish contract/schema validation from backward-compatibility evidence.
Name which provider/consumer refs are being compared.
Do not claim authorization, performance, or production readiness from contract compatibility alone.

fixtures.description: Deterministic CI reliability scenario with missing platform coverage and a soft-failed required validation gate.
constraints: Both intended OS legs are required validation evidence.
The required test command must be workflow-fatal when it fails.
Do not redesign the application tests themselves.
Do not expand the fix into production rollout or rollback strategy.

fixtures.description: Deterministic compatibility-claim scenario based on evidence that exists for Windows and Ubuntu tooling execution but not macOS or third-party runtime loading.

initial_state.observed_ci: GitHub-hosted windows-latest and ubuntu-latest both passed the repository suite with PowerShell Core 7.6.6
initial_state.unexecuted_runtime: third-party agent requiring a different discovery/index convention
initial_state.proposed_claim: The suite is fully cross-platform and works in compatible agent runtimes.

constraints: Do not invent macOS execution.
Do not convert vendor support into repository-tested support.
Keep runtime discovery/loading separate from repository tooling execution.
Record adaptation-required rather than drop-in compatibility for a mismatched runtime convention.
